english: A: King, hear my vow: I will drive a hundred horses to the ... (póyḱoybʰos). B: Your vow is great. What did you stake? A: My dear and swift horses. B: If you drive them there, your fame will be good. Fill my cup. A cup of bronze -- and may Perkwunos be with you.
uncertain: who says the last two sentences

english: A: Men, look! I take (eat?) from the mixing-bowl. Your vow is great, and your belly small. Look! He swallowed the whole... B: Now I lie on the ground. The earth turns. A: The earth does not turn; the mead turns in your head. Friends, carry me up (lift me).
uncertain: solh₂wóm gʷr̥h₃óm: 'whole' + participle/noun? 'he devoured the whole'

english: A: How many men are coming to the feast tonight? B: Ten men are coming, and their sisters and wives are also coming. A: Is there much mead in the house? B: There is not much. Your sister's mead is in the house; go to her. A: I go, and she gives it, if she loves me. B: Soon the guests will arrive in the evening.
uncertain: swésorm̥ toy gʷh₂dʰí: 'go to your sister' (acc. of goal)

english: A: King, my share is small. B: Why do you say so? A: Every man gets his own share. One gets a leg, and I get a bone. B: He killed a boar. If you kill a boar, you too will get a leg. A: Now I go early and hunt (track). B: Go, and may Perkwunos protect you.
uncertain: h₁éy tworḱóm gʷʰént: 'he went? killed a boar' -- h₁éy unclear (that one?)

english: A: Father, why do you pour mead into the fire? B: Fire carries it to the gods. Now they rejoice and give us cows and children. A: Do they drink the mead? B: They drink it and like the smoke of the meat. A: May I pour (libate) into the fire? B: Pour for my son, and praise father Dyeus.

A: Man, you are too drunk. How many cups have you drunk? B: I drank three cups; my host poured them for me. A: Three cups? You have drunk nine cups. B: When you are not angry(?), the mead is sweet. A: Tonight you will sleep with the dogs. B: Now I go to the dogs.
uncertain: gʷḗn mē gʰrémes: 'when you do not grumble/rage' (gʷḗn = 'when'?)
